statement.title: A ledger is a habit, not a chore
statement.text: Most stalls lose a morning a month to paper. Keep the receipt in your hand for three seconds longer and the morning is yours again.

steps.title: Three small things, in order.
steps.text: Nothing to learn and nothing to set up. The same three moves every market day.

items.title: Photograph the receipt
items.text: Snap it as you get it. Handwriting is read too, and what could not be read is marked for you.

items.title: Let it be sorted
items.text: Stock, rent, pay, fuel. Each line lands under its heading, and you can move any of them with a thumb.

items.title: Close the week
items.text: Read the week on one page, fix what is marked, and send the month to your accountant with one tap.

features.title: Everything a stall keeps, in one place
features.text: A ledger, not an accounting suite: what came in, what went out, and what the month made.

items.d: Printed or handwritten, in four languages. Each amount is shown beside the picture it came from.

items.t: A reminder that does not nag
items.d: One nudge on Sunday evening. Nothing else, ever.

plans.title: Two plans. No contract, either way.
plans.text: One lost morning costs more than a year of Stall. Begin free and move up when a second stall opens.

items.q: What does it cost to begin?
items.a: Nothing for the first month, and no card is asked for. After that Stall is €9 a month and Row is €29.

items.q: Can I take my books with me?
items.a: At any time: every line and every picture, as CSV and a folder of images.
